accepted_step.derivation: Re-derivation of step 2 from the prose and accepted step 1. Let X_1,...,X_12 be the input bits. The givens state that they are independent and that for each i, P(X_i=1)=3/5 and P(X_i=0)=2/5. Independence means that for any fixed assignment x_1,...,x_12 in {0,1}^12, P(X_1=x_1,...,X_12=x_12)=product_{i=1}^{12} P(X_i=x_i). If the fixed string has exactly seven 1s and five 0s, then exactly seven factors are 3/5 and exactly five factors are 2/5. Finite multiplication is commutative and associative, so the product is (3/5)^7(2/5)^5, independent of which positions contain the 1s. The deterministic transitions F_0 and F_1 from step 1 act only after each bit is read and do not change the probability law or independence of the input string; they only determine the final state for each string. Thus every fixed length-12 string with exactly seven 1s has the same probability.
accepted_step.goal: Use independence of the twelve bits to show each fixed length-12 string with exactly seven 1s has probability (3/5)^7(2/5)^5, independent of the positions of the 1s.
accepted_step.result: Each fixed length-12 bit string with exactly seven 1s has probability (3/5)^7(2/5)^5, independent of the positions of the 1s.
